subject: genetics
question: **Type:** concept A man is described as hemizygous at the *F8* locus on the X chromosome. What does hemizygosity mean at this locus?

options.text: He has only one allele at the locus, because his single X chromosome has no homolog on the Y chromosome
He carries two copies of the same allele, one on each X chromosome
He carries one allele on the X chromosome and a matching allele on the Y chromosome
He has no functional allele at the locus, because his single X chromosome is inactivated as a Barr body

explanation: Males carry one X and one Y chromosome, and the Y chromosome has no allele at the *F8* locus, so a male has exactly one copy of the gene and is hemizygous; any allele he carries is expressed. B describes a homozygous condition that requires two X chromosomes, C wrongly assumes matching alleles on the Y chromosome, and D confuses hemizygosity with the X inactivation that occurs in female cells.
